fixture.note: Real bytes from ONE run on this machine (CPU, release build, GPU engine not linked). A tiny WALDO chatml-v1 model was trained (SFT on our own tool-call conversations, run-inputs/conversations.jsonl) and exported with tokenizer.json and the standard ChatML template. The AIEN daemon loaded it. AIEN own generation path (StreamTurn) on that loaded model produced the tool-call text, and the DAEMON wrote its own generation record (ledger-generation.json, id returned in TurnFinished.generation_record) carrying the model and tokenizer digests, the output text digest and its own pid and start time. The INTERPLANE aien_legacy dialect parsed that text into the request; the adapter then drove one approved write_file and the daemon wrote its ledger records. Limits (docs/DAEMON_GENERATION_RECORD.md in sovereign-core 12c1a5f): the digests are of the files read at load time (a swap between hash and load is not detected), the record is not signed (a same-user process that can append to the compose ledger could forge one), request_id/operation_id are the client claims, and no capability or authority follows. The model is a tiny memoriser with a fixed prompt: no capability claim. The adapter is the merged INTERPLANE adapter at interplane main c982fd3 (interplane#81, re-pinned to sovereign-core 4d4dfd4, signs the requirements goal). Scope: CPU only, no GPU and no native OS; the tiny model is a memoriser; none of this is authority.
